chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:
Beware of Al-Tihaf Al-Samma'. I said, 'And what is Al-Tihaf Al-Samma?' He said: 'To insert the garment from beneath your arm and place it on one shoulder.'

key_terms.الصَّمَّاءِ: A specific style of draping, often described as covering the back and one shoulder while leaving the other arm free.
key_terms.الْتِحَافُ: The act of draping or wrapping a garment over the shoulder.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Al-Tihaf Al-Samma' in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific draping style of 'Al-Tihaf Al-Samma'', where the garment is tucked under the arm to rest on one shoulder, a practice often associated with the pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah or specific cultural norms of the time. It serves as a legal distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity and etiquette of prayer attire, emphasizing modesty and proper coverage over mere functionality. The ruling highlights the importance of distinguishing between acceptable prayer garments and those that may be considered imitative of non-Muslim customs or insufficiently modest.
